messages:
Maya (support): escalating a customer production issue: embeddings endpoint returning mixed vector sizes for a single batch call. They switched from text-embedding-3-small -> text-embedding-3-large and now one item in the batch is 512 while the others are 1536. Downstream vector DB ingestion fails (validate-length strict).

Maya (support): customer payload/logs they sent: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Body: {\"model\":\"text-embedding-3-large\", \"input\": [\"a\", \"b\", \"c\"]}
Response: 200 OK
embeddings: [ [..512 floats..], [..1536 floats..], [..1536 floats..] ]
Downstream error: \"expected 1536 got 512\"
```
They say this started right after upgrading our Python SDK from 0.9.1 -> 0.9.2 and it only happens for batched calls (single-item calls always return 1536).

Leo (eng-ml): dimension mismatch usually means mixed-model output. Possible causes: client accidentally varying model per item, SDK-level transparent fallback that switches model on per-item retry, or a server routing bug that merged items from different model backends into one batch response. Batching should be atomic model-wise.

Anjali (devex): ask for raw response headers and the exact SDK version + snippet of their call. Also ask if they use any custom per-item metadata that could change model selection.

Maya (support): they confirmed Python SDK v0.9.2 and provided this minimal repro (sanitized):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"REDACTED\")
texts = [\"short\", \"normal length text\", \"another\"]
res = client.embeddings.create(model=\"text-embedding-3-large\", input=texts, batch_size=8, timeout=10)
# iterate res.data and push to vector DB
```
They observe len(res.data[0]) == 512, others 1536.

Sam (sdk-python): I'll bisect changes between 0.9.1 and 0.9.2. Look for any per-item retry/fallback or altered default model settings. Also check transit headers we attach for debugging (we might not be surfacing model-per-item today).

Kai (sdk-ts): server should never mix models in one batch. If a per-item fallback happened on the server, the response should either fail the batch or tag which item used a fallback. We currently don't return per-item model identifiers in the payload; adding that would help debug.

Maya (support): provided request-id rq_3aX9YQ for the problematic call. Forwarding to eng.

Ops-bot: logs request queued, retrieving routing traces for rq_3aX9YQ (ETA ~ 10m).

Leo (eng-ml): I pulled the routing/worker logs. We see a transient decode failure on the large model for item index 0; server retried that item on the small model as an availability fallback, then stitched results into the original batch response. This is a regression: batch responses must be homogeneous.

Sam (sdk-python): Confirmed. Root cause is server-side per-item fallback. Immediate mitigations: 
1) Server: disable per-item fallback for batch endpoints (hotfix)
2) Client: defensive check for embedding length before writing to DB + single-item retry logic.

Anjali (devex): I'll draft a KB titled 'Embeddings: dimension mismatch after SDK upgrade' with repro + mitigation snippets and link it to the support ticket.

Sam (sdk-python): quick client-side Python validation snippet to share with customer:
```python
EXPECTED = 1536
resp = client.embeddings.create(model=\"text-embedding-3-large\", input=texts)
clean = []
for i, item in enumerate(resp.data):
    vec = item
    if len(vec) != EXPECTED:
        # try a single-item retry with longer timeout
        retry = client.embeddings.create(model=\"text-embedding-3-large\", input=[texts[i]], timeout=30)
        vec2 = retry.data[0]
        if len(vec2) != EXPECTED:
            # escalate: persistent mismatch
            raise RuntimeError(f\"embedding length mismatch after retry idx={i}\")
        clean.append(vec2)
    else:
        clean.append(vec)
# safe to push 'clean' to vector DB
```

Kai (sdk-ts): TS version with explicit timeout/backoff for concurrent batching: 
```ts
const EXPECTED = 1536;
const res = await client.embeddings.create({model: 'text-embedding-3-large', input: texts});
for (let i = 0; i < res.data.length; i++) {
  if (res.data[i].length !== EXPECTED) {
    const retry = await client.embeddings.create({model: 'text-embedding-3-large', input: [texts[i]], timeout: 20000});
    if (retry.data[0].length !== EXPECTED) {
      throw new Error(`embedding mismatch for idx ${i}`);
    }
  }
}
```

Leo (eng-ml): Hotfix plan (P0/P1): 
- P0: roll back per-item fallback behavior for batch requests and deploy strict model-homogeneity in the batch response assembler (ETA ~6 hours).
- P1: add per-item `model_used` field in the embedding response and emit it in headers for immediate reconciliation.
- P1: server-side validation option to reject a batch if items came from different model variants (config flag).

Maya (support): customer worried about billing: they were charged large-model token rates, but some items were served by small model. Finance needs per-item billing trace.

Leo (eng-ml): we'll export per-item routing trace for rq_3aX9YQ and mark which model served which item to feed finance. Sam, can the service quickly include a per-item annotation in the logs/response for this request id?

Sam (sdk-python): yes, I'll add a temporary `model_used` property on each embedding object in the response for the affected request so finance can reconcile charges. Also adding an SDK warning when embedding lengths differ. I'll queue SDK patch 0.9.3 with those changes and a stricter default retry/backoff for embeddings.

Anjali (devex): KB will include: repro, quick validation snippets (py/ts), guidance to set batch_size=1 as a short-term mitigation if customers can't run validation, and contact steps for billing reconciliation.

Maya (support): customer accepted the validation+retry workaround and asked for ETA on the server hotfix and billing reconciliation. I informed them of the 6-hour ETA and that finance will follow up.

Jordan (support-bot): MM created and assigned to Leo + Sam. :white_check_mark:

Leo (eng-ml): I'll update once the hotfix is deployed. After deployment we should run a smoke test across typical batch sizes and longer sequences to ensure no regressions and confirm metrics (error rates, latency) are stable.

Maya (support): closing loop for now: ticket created for finance, KB draft started, customer given workaround. Thanks all :sparkles:
